correctness.rationale: The random-poset Fraïssé extension identifies each nonalgebraic one-type with a compatible ideal L and filter U of the finite parameter poset. For graph incidence P_H, downsets are formed by choosing vertex subset A and any subset of edge points wholly supported by A, giving Z_H=Σ_A 2^{e_H(A)}. Nonempty L,U require L to be one lower vertex with a nonempty incident-edge upper subset, or exactly the two endpoints of a unique edge with U that edge, yielding Σ_v(2^{deg v}-1)+|E|. The single-empty-side cases total 2Z_H-1. For each missing-edge family F, Δ_F 2^{e_{H∪S}(A)}=2^{e_H(A)}∏_{f∈F}(2^{1_{f⊂A}}−1), equal to 2^{e_H(A)} iff V(F)⊂A and zero otherwise. The vertex-degree contribution is nonzero exactly for v common to every new edge and the linear |E| term contributes precisely at |F|=1. This proves the exact Δ_F formula and strict positivity from A=V for every order, including n=0 boundaries when no F exists. Möbius inversion at E=∅ gives the claimed all-positive coefficients. Crown ideals are antichains of a 2m-cycle, counted by known Lucas L_{2m}. Inspected actual verification script; separate ternary-extension enumeration reproduced all 76 labeled graph cases n≤4 and a second-order difference of 10 for a disjoint-edge test; these tests are not the all-size proof.

value.rationale: The family of naturally marked graph incidence posets offers a structural quantification of how adding new edge parameters changes available complete types. The theorem gives simultaneous strictly positive mixed derivatives in every order with exact coefficients, a nontrivial global qualitative property not captured by one count or a crown formula; it is mathematically motivated by the insertion operation and useful for order-theoretic type-growth comparisons. No complexity improvement or novel Lucas identity is claimed.

limitations: Finite simple graphs with a fixed labeled vertex set; inserting a missing graph edge creates a new named upper parameter, not a comparability among existing points.
Crown Lucas count is prior mathematics; 76 finite checks do not establish all-order positivity.
